Theon's Oak Green Porsche 911 Looks Like The Perfect Driver's Car

TB
By Tyler Brooks Viral Concepts & Prototype Lead • via Carscoops Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Carscoops Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Theon Design has established itself as one of the most recognizable names in the Porsche 911 restomodding scene, and its latest creation might just be the most impressive it's built to date.
  • This stunning, one-off commission perfectly combines new materials, an updated design, and a serious powertrain and chassis setup to create what looks like the ultimate driver's car.
  • Official reporting verified via Carscoops news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • TYLER BROOKS Viral Concepts & Prototype Lead

Automotive Innovation & Market Feasibility

Concept prototypes and viral vehicle reveals offer an exciting window into the automotive industry's future design language. Dispatches from Carscoops demonstrate how radical styling, lightweight materials, and powertrain packaging can transition from design studios to production assembly lines. Engineering feasibility and homologation standards remain the true measures of impact.

Big Picture: Market reception and formal OEM production announcements will determine which concept innovations make it to consumer streets.

Theon Design has established itself as one of the most recognizable names in the Porsche 911 restomodding scene, and its latest creation might just be the most impressive it's built to date. This stunning, one-off commission perfectly combines new materials, an updated design, and a serious powertrain and chassis setup to create what looks like the ultimate driver's car.

📌 The Core Development

Like other projects from Theon Design , this one started with a 964-generation 911 getting stripped back to its bare shell, and then custom carbon fiber body panels were fitted. These new carbon panels strip away roughly 661 lbs (300 kg) from the car and have been painted in a lovely shade of Oak Green Neo Metallic, which is inspired by Porsche's own shade of Oak Green Metallic. Making the car stand out further are a champagne-colored Porsche script and matching 17-inch champagne wheels and brake calipers.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Unlike some others in this field, such as Gunther Werks , Theon Design hasn't chased modern supercar power figures with its reborn 911. It uses a modified naturally aspirated 4.0-liter air-cooled flat-six with 419 horsepower and 322 pound-feet of torque. Those are some serious figures considering the car only weighs 2,535 lbs (1,150 kg). Modern conveniences like drive-by-wire and selectable engine maps have also been added. The engine operates alongside a five-speed manual transmission driving the rear wheels. It also rocks brake discs and calipers from a 993-generation Carrera RS.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Theon Design's upgrades don't stop with fresh bodywork, paint, and an upgraded engine. This car, like all its others, features an overhauled chassis that comes with semi-active TracTive dampers with custom spring rates designed specifically for British roads. It's also been fitted with Michelin Pilot Sport tires with tall sidewalls to boost ride quality.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

The interior is also rather special. A set of Recaro CS seats is now fitted up front and wrapped in lovely light-brown leather. This leather continues across the rear seats, door panels, the transmission tunnel, and the lower half of the dashboard. Other surfaces are wrapped in black leather with brown contrast stitching. Theon's attention to detail extends to milled aluminum window switches, a modern climate-control system, and a custom wiring loom that alone saves 55 lbs (25 kg). Unlike a current 911, there are no screens in sight, as this car is all about delivering the purest expression of driving possible.

The British firm will soon have a special 911-based model that's even more exhilarating than this one promises to be. It's working on a new R-branded lineup where models will use a 4.0-liter flat-six with over 500 hp. These models will also go on an even stricter diet and weigh less than 2,200 lbs (1,000 kg). Prices for a 'basic' model like this Oak Green Neo Metallic car start at £435,000 ($576,000).
